The bottom of the powerhouse discharge structure is at elevation 1,050 feet or about 60 feet above the bottom of the Whitewater River Cove.
To provide for flow augmentation to Howard Creek, a steel pipe would be embedded in concrete under the Bad Creek Dam; intakes for the pipe would be located at elevations of 2,120, 2,230, and 2,280 feet (190, 80, and 30 feet below full pool elevation, respectively). Flow through the pipe would be through a control valve and an aerator. A larger pipe would discharge natural runoff from the basin during construction and would be plugged upon completion of construction. The flow augmentation system would be used only if water quality in the upper reservoir is adequate for such use.
Since the proposed upper reservoir would experience severe fluctuations, Applicant intends to prohibit public use of project lands and waters as a safety precaution, and proposes to provide off-site recreation developments instead. A general plan has been submitted for a 31-mile hiking trail between the lower Whitewater Falls area and the Pinnacle Mountain area in Table Rock State Park on non-project lands owned by the Crescent Land and Timber Corporation (Figure 1-8).
At least three shelters and other features would be developed along the proposed hiking trail. The proposed trail would comprise a central link in the proposed Foothills Trail, which will ultimately join the Table Rock and Oconee State Park areas. The Applicant's portion of the trail apparently would connect with several short segments to be developed by the U.S. Forest Service in the Whitewater River Unit of the Nantahala National Forest in North Carolina. The Foothills Trail would then extend southwest through the Keowee Unit of the Sumter National Forest to Stumphouse Mountain Tunnel Park, about 5 miles south of Oconee State Park (Forest Service, NDb).
